# Mod content policy

*This policy covers every mod, race, scenario, art or sound pack and share code made for this game, wherever the project shows, links or lists it.*

## 1. Making mods

You may make mods for this game and share them for free. You keep the rights to your work.

When the project lists your mod, you allow it to host the mod and to adapt it so it keeps working with new game versions. If mod.json sets allowFeature, you also allow the project to show the mod's name, pictures and short clips in its news, with credit to you.

## 2. Your own work

Share only what you made or may share. List every outside source with its author and licence in the sources field of mod.json.

## 3. Nothing from other games

Do not include names, pictures, music, sounds, text, logos or other material from other games or media unless you hold the rights to it. That includes material taken from game files by extraction, conversion or AI. Mods that bring back another game's content are not listed or supported.

## 4. Not official

Do not present a mod as made, approved or endorsed by the project or by any studio.

## 5. Never allowed

Illegal content, sexual content, hate, harassment or threats, content aimed at real people or sharing their private details, and content that promotes terrorism or self-harm.

## 6. Fit for the game's players

A mod must suit the same players as the game itself. There is no mature-content switch.

## 7. Data only

A mod holds data, pictures, sound and text. No code, no attempts to break the game's loader, no tracking, and no links that download files from elsewhere.

## 8. Generative AI

Say in mod.json (aiUse) what you made with generative AI. Do not use a real person's likeness, prompts that name a living artist's style, or other games' art as AI input.

## 9. Free mods

Mods are free: no paywalls and no paid early access. One link to your own donation page is fine.

## 10. Credits and remixes

Credit the mods you build on (basedOn in mod.json) and respect their licences. The mod template suggests CC-BY-4.0 for content and MIT for code.

## 11. Reporting a mod

Use the report link of the mod catalog, or write to the contact address on the catalog page. Say which mod and version, what is wrong and where.

## 12. What the project does

The project may remove a mod from its lists and tells the author why. Authors who break this policy again and again can be refused. An author can reply to appeal.

## 13. Safety for players

The game loads mods as data only and shows each mod's hashes. You can remove a mod at any time; your saves are kept apart from your mods.

## 14. Changes

This policy may change. The version in the game and in the mod template is the current one.
